reports.title: Full Truck Alliance Co. Ltd. Announces Third Quarter 2026 Unaudited Financial Results

guidance.heading: Business Outlook
section: The Company expects its total net revenues to be between RMB3.19 billion and RMB3.29 billion for the fourth quarter of 2026, representing approximately flat to a 3.1% year-over-year increase. These forecasts are based on the Company’s current and preliminary view of the market and operational conditions, which are subject to change and cannot be predicted with reasonable accuracy as of the date hereof.

desk.headline: Revenue up 6.8% to RMB3.59bn, ahead of estimates; adjusted profit up 47%; Q4 revenue seen flat to up 3.1%
results: Revenue rose 6.8% to RMB3.59bn, about 8% above the RMB3.31bn estimate, as fees on matched freight orders grew 25%.
Adjusted earnings of RMB1.38 per ADS beat the RMB1.32 estimate and rose from RMB0.93; net income was up 49% to RMB1.37bn.
Value-added services revenue fell to RMB331.3m from RMB560.7m as the company shrinks its lending business; the loan book halved to RMB2.5bn.
The bad-loan ratio rose to 4.7% from 2.9% at end-2025, partly because the loan book shrank quickly.
Operating cash flow almost doubled to RMB3.16bn; cash and investments reached RMB35.5bn, and a US$0.084-per-ADS dividend was declared.

guidance.summary: For Q4 2026 the company expects revenue of RMB3.19–3.29bn, roughly flat to 3.1% higher than a year earlier, which is slower than Q3's 6.8% growth.

points: Order growth slowed slightly from Q2, which management put down to typhoons, heavy rain and the timing of the Mid-Autumn Festival.
With commissions now charged on about 95% of eligible orders, future fee growth must come from more orders, finer route pricing and premium services.
New trucker subsidies, booked as a reduction in commission revenue, held back transaction revenue growth this quarter.
Overseas app Qmove now runs in five markets; daily orders doubled from Q2 and commissions began in Indonesia, the UAE and Turkey.
Management flagged extreme weather, fuel-price swings and a tough economy as the main risks to trucker activity.
